nodes.name: Hydrothermal Mo precursor deposition
nodes.procedure: (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O (740 mg) was separately dispersed in 80 mL of deionized (DI) water. The mixture was transferred into an autoclave, and a piece of NF (4.5 cm × 4.5 cm) was vertically immersed into the solution and kept at 150 °C for 6 h. Then, Mo-based oxides were collected and dried.

nodes.name: Carbothermal shocking reduction
nodes.procedure: Then, a rapid carbothermal shocking method (Joule-heat equipment: Hefei in situ technology Co., Ltd. China) and hydrogen reduction were applied to prepare MoO2/NF. A piece of Mo-based oxides (1 cm × 2 cm) was heated at 800 °C on a graphite heating plate for 133 seconds under Ar-H2 flow (Fig. S1, ESI†), and then, MoO2/NF (mass loading ∼5 mg cm^-2) was collected.

nodes.name: Anodic reconstruction to FeMoOOH
nodes.procedure: A typical three-electrode system was used to prepare FeMoOOH/NF (Fig. S2, ESI†). Among them, a carbon rod and a Hg/HgO electrode (SCE) were used as the counter electrode and the reference electrode, respectively. Then, MoO2/NF was placed in 1.0 M KOH solution with 0.28 mM Fe(NO3)3·9H2O as the working electrode. Subsequently, electrochemical anodic reconstruction was performed at a constant voltage (0.87 V vs. Hg/HgO) of 2 h to obtain the amorphous FeMoOOH/NF electrocatalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows Mo leaching of 4.2 mg L^-1 for FeMoOOH/NF and 8.7 mg L^-1 for MoOx/NF after 2 h reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) test showed that the Mo content in the electrolyte was 8.7 mg L^-1 after 2 hours of testing. ... The corresponding Mo content in the electrolyte solution was 4.2 mg L^-1.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows FeMoOOH/NF is amorphous with disappearance of original MoO2 peaks after reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) of FeMoOOH/NF with different reconstruction times (0 h, 0.5 h and 2 h) revealed that the crystal structure of FeMoOOH/NF was significantly altered and the original MoO2 peaks disappeared.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows FeMoOOH/NF evolves from dense nanosheet structure at 0 h to loose surface structure at 0.5 h and deep reconstructed structure at 2 h.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface morphology of FeMoOOH/NF was studied using scanning electron microscopy (SEM)/ex situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms amorphous nanosheet structure of FeMoOOH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Fig. 2g) showed a nanosheet structure. An amorphous state structure of FeMoOOH/NF (Fig. 2g and h) was consistent with the XRD results.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms amorphous structure of FeMoOOH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: An amorphous state structure of FeMoOOH/NF (Fig. 2g and h) was consistent with the XRD results.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows uniform distribution of Mo, O, and Fe in amorphous FeMoOOH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping images (Fig. 2i and j) of FeMoOOH/NF revealed the uniform distribution of Mo, O and Fe.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Mo=O peak at 891 cm^-1 for MoO4^2-, Mo–O–Mo/Fe at 797 cm^-1, and M–OOH peaks at 472 and 552 cm^-1 in FeMoOOH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy was performed from 0 to 2 h to investigate the dynamic reconstruction process of FeMoOOH/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo 3d shifts from Mo^4+ (229.6/233.6 eV) to Mo^6+ (232.3/235.6 eV); O 1s shows Mo–O–Fe bond at 531.5 eV increasing to 33.5% at 2 h; Fe 2p shows Fe^3+ at 708.8/720.4 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The two peaks (Fig. 3d) in the Mo 3d spectrum in MoO2/NF were from Mo^4+ (229.6/233.6 eV) ... as the reconstruction time increased, the peak of Mo^4+ completely converted into the more stable Mo^6+. ... a new Mo–O–Fe bond peak was found at 531.5 eV, which gradually increased from 27.8% (0.5 h) to 33.5% (2 h).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows stable Fe:Mo mole ratio of 3:7 in FeMoOOH/NF after reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the corresponding ICP test (Fig. 3g) of FeMoOOH/NF from 0 to 2 h exhibited that the mole ratio of Fe : Mo was about 3 : 7 and then it remained stable.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl of FeMoOOH/NF is 469 mF cm^-2, higher than MoOx/NF (275 mF cm^-2), indicating high ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FeMoOOH/NF had a higher double-layer capacitance (Cdl) value (469 mF cm^-2) than MoOx/NF (275 mF cm^-2), suggesting that the deep reconstructed FeMoOOH/NF possessed a high electrochemically active surface area (ECSA).
